note: Every entry must name an owner and an expiry condition that some other party can observe. A permanent exemption is not allowed: if a split cannot expire, the correct outcome is a code change, not an entry here. `majors` lists the compatibility buckets observed inside the core protocol repositories; a NEW major outside this list re-opens the finding.

openmls-0.9-rustcrypto-generation.summary: openmls 0.9 ships openmls_rust_crypto 0.6 / openmls_basic_credential 0.6 / hpke-rs-rust-crypto 0.7, all still on the RustCrypto 0.10/0.12 generation and on dalek 2.x. Every SDK consumer that enables MLS inherits the old line beside the SDK's own 0.11/3.x line.
openmls-0.9-rustcrypto-generation.expires_when: openmls publishes a release whose openmls_rust_crypto and openmls_basic_credential depend on digest 0.11 / sha2 0.11 / aes-gcm 0.11 / hkdf 0.13 and ed25519-dalek 3.
openmls-0.9-rustcrypto-generation.verify: python arkret-rust-sdk/tools/dep_matrix.py --why ed25519-dalek  (the 2.x column must lose its openmls_* dependents)

coauth-jose-pkcs8-generation.summary: coauth-keyring has a multi-algorithm in-process PrivateKey enum requiring one shared pkcs8 type across RSA / P-256 / P-384 / P-521 / K-256 / Ed25519. rsa 0.9, p384 0.13, p521 0.13 and k256 0.13 have no release on the pkcs8 0.11 / elliptic-curve 0.14 / signature 3.0 generation, so the whole der/spki/const-oid/sec1/ecdsa/generic-array family and everything feature-coupled to it stays a generation behind.
coauth-jose-pkcs8-generation.expires_when: rsa, p384, p521 and k256 all publish releases on elliptic-curve 0.14 / pkcs8 0.11 / signature 3.0. p256 0.14.0 already exists, so the generation has started.
coauth-jose-pkcs8-generation.verify: python arkret-rust-sdk/tools/dep_matrix.py --why elliptic-curve  (coauth must resolve 0.14 only)
coauth-jose-pkcs8-generation.correction: Reviewed 2026-10-11: Coauth's manifest identifies the remaining shared PKCS#8 blockers as RSA/P-384/P-521/K-256. The independent Encrypter axis now uses chacha20poly1305 0.11 / aead 0.6; it does not wait for this family.

salvo-0.96-cookie-0.18.summary: salvo 0.96 (pinned =0.96.0 in six repositories) depends on cookie 0.18, which still uses aes-gcm 0.10, sha2 0.10, hkdf 0.12, hmac 0.12, rand 0.8 and base64 0.22.
salvo-0.96-cookie-0.18.expires_when: salvo publishes a release on cookie 0.19 or later, or drops the cookie dependency from the feature set the servers enable.
salvo-0.96-cookie-0.18.verify: python arkret-work/tools/dep_matrix.py --why aes-gcm  (cookie must disappear from the 0.10 column)

dioxus-0.7.10-fullstack.summary: dioxus is pinned exactly at =0.7.10 in inkson, coauth, flagon and codmin. dioxus-fullstack 0.7.10 pulls reqwest 0.12, gloo-net 0.6, gloo-utils 0.2 and base64 0.22; dioxus-web pulls gloo-timers 0.3; dioxus-desktop pulls rand 0.9 and (through tao/wry) windows 0.61.
dioxus-0.7.10-fullstack.expires_when: dioxus publishes a release whose dioxus-fullstack depends on reqwest 0.13 and gloo-net 0.7, and the exact pin is moved to it in all four consumers at once.
dioxus-0.7.10-fullstack.verify: python arkret-work/tools/dep_matrix.py --why reqwest  (dioxus-fullstack must disappear from the 0.12 column)

wasm-getrandom-feature-alias.summary: arkret-rust-sdk and inkson deliberately declare a second getrandom line under the alias getrandom_02 so the wasm32 `js` backend can be enabled on the 0.2 copy that ring / rand_core 0.6 / redox_users drag in. This is an intentional feature-unification alias, not an accidental duplicate, and the manifests say so.
wasm-getrandom-feature-alias.expires_when: no dependency in any core repository resolves getrandom 0.2 any more; at that point the getrandom_02 alias must be deleted rather than kept.

legacy-phf-rand-0.7.summary: phf_generator 0.8 (reached through the dioxus desktop tree) is the only consumer of rand 0.7 / rand_core 0.5 / getrandom 0.1 anywhere in the workspace. It is a build-time string-hash generator with no cryptographic role.
legacy-phf-rand-0.7.expires_when: the dependency chain reaching phf_generator 0.8 upgrades to phf 0.11 or later.
legacy-phf-rand-0.7.verify: python arkret-work/tools/dep_matrix.py --why rand  (the 0.7 column must be empty)

exemptions.reason: 3.0.0 is the Arkret SDK protocol line. 2.2.0 remains in OpenMLS and in coauth-jose/coauth-keyring's shared PKCS#8 generation. coauth-backend declares dalek 2 plus the ed25519-dalek-3 alias, with raw seed/public-key crossings confined to arkret_key_bridge.rs. coauth-storage-postgres directly declares only the SDK-generation alias; it has no dalek-2 bridge. Other generations can remain transitively in its graph.
exemptions.expires_when: both families expire. The coauth half is the one that can move first.
exemptions.risk: The bridge is byte-for-byte safe today because Ed25519 raw keys are version-independent, but two SigningKey types in one crate is a standing hazard: any future code path that hands a dalek-2 key to a dalek-3 verifier fails to compile, and any path that skips the round trip silently uses the wrong RNG generation.

exemptions.reason: arkret-crypto, hpke 0.14 and x-wing use 3.0.0. hpke-rs-rust-crypto 0.7 (the openmls provider) is the sole consumer of 2.0.1.

0.11.0 is declared by ten of eleven core repositories. coauth is the only repository that declares 0.10.9, with the `oid` feature, because its PKCS#8 keystore needs the OID associations from the elliptic-curve 0.13 generation. The remaining 0.10 consumers everywhere else are cookie 0.18, ed25519-dalek 2.2.0, p256/p384 0.13 and voprf.
exemptions.expires_when: family coauth-jose-pkcs8-generation expires for the declaration; the transitive copies expire with the openmls and salvo families.
exemptions.risk: Digest crates are the one place where a version split is not merely cosmetic: an event digest computed with a mismatched Sha256 impl would be silently wrong. Both lines produce identical bytes, so the exposure is compile-time trait mismatch rather than wrong output - but that must be re-verified, not assumed, before any bump.

exemptions.reason: coauth is the only core repository that declares digest at all (0.10.7). Everywhere else both majors are transitive, following whichever sha2/hmac/ecdsa generation pulled them.
Eight core repositories declare 0.13.0; coauth declares 0.12.1 because rfc6979 0.4 / hkdf 0.12 / cookie 0.18 in its graph require it.
Five core repositories declare 0.13.0. 0.12.4 exists only transitively, through elliptic-curve 0.13 and cookie 0.18.
Every core repository that declares aes-gcm declares 0.11.1. 0.10.3 arrives only through cookie 0.18, hpke-rs-rust-crypto 0.7 and openmls_rust_crypto 0.6.

Coauth's Encrypter now declares 0.11.0 with alloc only, independently of its JOSE PKCS#8 family. The 0.10 line remains transitively through OpenMLS / hpke-rs-rust-crypto; it is not an Encrypter requirement.
exemptions.expires_when: The OpenMLS/hpke RustCrypto dependency family moves off chacha20poly1305 0.10. Confirm with tools/dep_matrix.py --why chacha20poly1305; do not remove the exemption merely because all first-party declarations agree.
exemptions.risk: The accepted Coauth upgrade preserves Base64(nonce12 || ciphertext || tag16) for OAuth client/provider secrets and encoded Apple credentials. Legacy-generated fixed fixtures, independent OpenSSL comparison, database reads and actual credential adapters verify this axis. PKCS#8 private-key encryption and the SDK XChaCha20 encrypted-file vault are separate boundaries.

exemptions.reason: arkret-signatures and floria declare 0.14.0. coauth declares 0.13.2 because it must share one elliptic-curve generation with p384, p521 and k256, none of which have a 0.14 release. openmls_basic_credential and hpke-rs-rust-crypto also pin 0.13.
arkret-rust-sdk and cotest declare 0.6.0. coauth declares 0.5.3 because password-hash 0.5 is shared with pkcs5 0.7 / scrypt 0.11 / pbkdf2 0.12, which the pkcs8 `encryption` feature requires.
exemptions.risk: argon2 is coauth's password hashing primitive. A major bump must be validated against stored PHC strings, not only against fresh hashes.

exemptions.reason: bridges declares 0.11; coauth declares 0.10.6, following the digest 0.10 generation its JOSE stack is pinned to.

coland, floria and flagon declare 0.10.2. coauth declares 0.8.5 because ed25519-dalek 2's `rand_core` feature and its key-generation calls are on the rand_core 0.6 generation. flagon additionally declares a second line under the alias rand_09. 0.9 arrives through proptest, sentry, tungstenite and opentelemetry_sdk; 0.7 only through phf_generator 0.8.
exemptions.expires_when: the coauth half expires with family coauth-jose-pkcs8-generation; flagon's rand_09 alias must be removed when its consumer moves to 0.10; the 0.9 tier expires as proptest / sentry / opentelemetry release on rand 0.10.

exemptions.reason: Four core repositories declare 0.10.1. coauth declares 0.6.4 alongside 0.10.1 (aliased rand_core_10) for the same dalek-2 reason as rand.
exemptions.expires_when: family coauth-jose-pkcs8-generation expires; the 0.5 tier expires with legacy-phf-rand-0.7.
exemptions.risk: rand_core is the RNG trait boundary. Two generations in one crate means a key-generation call can compile against the wrong CryptoRng without any diagnostic; every coauth key-generation site must be re-read when the alias is removed, not just recompiled.

exemptions.reason: SDK, coland and cotest declare 0.10.0. coauth declares both 0.3.1 and 0.10.0 (aliased rand_chacha_10) because its deterministic test and audit RNGs are typed against rand_core 0.6.

0.4.3 is the declared line everywhere. 0.2 is declared a second time on purpose (getrandom_02) so the wasm32 `js` backend can be turned on for the copy ring / rand_core 0.6 / redox_users pull in. 0.3 is the openmls-owned line. 0.1 reaches only cotest and inkson through phf_generator 0.8.
exemptions.expires_when: all three families expire; the getrandom_02 alias must be deleted at that point, not carried forward.

exemptions.reason: All ten declaring core repositories agree on 0.23.1; there is no first-party disagreement. 0.22.1 arrives through reqwest, hyper-util, headers, cookie, postgres-protocol and dioxus-fullstack. 0.21.7 reaches only coauth, through webauthn-rs 0.5 / base64urlsafedata 0.5.
exemptions.expires_when: the 0.22 tier expires as hyper-util / headers / cookie move to 0.23; the 0.21 tier expires when webauthn-rs releases on base64 0.22 or later.

exemptions.reason: Ten core repositories declare 0.13.4 and there is no first-party disagreement. 0.12.28 exists only because dioxus-fullstack 0.7.10 depends on it (and, in bridges, because serenity 0.12 and teloxide-core 0.13 do).
exemptions.expires_when: family dioxus-0.7.10-fullstack expires; the bridges half expires when serenity and teloxide release on reqwest 0.13.
exemptions.risk: Two reqwest generations mean two TLS backends can be linked at once. The egress policy in arkret-egress-reqwest only wraps the 0.13 line, so any code path that reaches the 0.12 client bypasses it. Today no first-party code holds a 0.12 client, and that must stay true.

exemptions.reason: codmin and flagon's admin UI declare 0.7.0. 0.6.0 comes only from dioxus-fullstack 0.7.10.
Transitive only: gloo-net 0.7 brings 0.3, gloo-net 0.6 (from dioxus-fullstack) brings 0.2.
Five core repositories declare 0.4. 0.3 comes from dioxus-web 0.7.10, dioxus-sdk-time and backon.

Every first-party Arkret workspace declares Salvo 1.0.1. Coland conformance-harness also resolves the external Savfox gateway on 0.96 and its third-party matrix-bot-sdk 0.2.4 on 0.89. These HTTP frameworks do not exchange Salvo request/response values with Arkret; protocol crossings use SDK DTOs and HTTP. This exception covers those resolved external trees, not a direct first-party version disagreement.
exemptions.expires_when: Savfox gateway and rmcp-client move to Salvo 1, and matrix-bot-sdk publishes or removes its Salvo 0.89 server dependency; then regenerate the Coland lock and remove this entry.
